chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pick up the pebbles and do not break any part of them.' The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'If he is able to perform wudu, let him perform wudu; and if he is not able, his ghusl suffices for him. And throwing (the pebbles) is not valid for him unless he is in a state of purity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ritual purity and handling of pebbles during the stoning of Jamarat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Basir, highlighting the specific etiquette of collecting pebbles (*hassat*) at Muzdalifah for the stoning of the Jamarat. The text clarifies that the pebbles must be gathered whole without breaking them, and establishes that the validity of the *Ramy* (throwing) is contingent upon maintaining ritual purity (*taharah*), where *wudu* is preferred but *ghusl* suffices if necessary.
